en-US.description: Modern sounding analysis and SHARPpy-style rendering for Python 3.11+, Qt6/PySide6, UWyo, ERA5, and WRF workflows.
en-US.longDescription: SHARPpy Reimagined - Modern sounding analysis and SHARPpy-style rendering for Python 3.11+. SHARPpy Reimagined is a modernized, standalone fork of SHARPpy, focused on packageable Python 3.11+ workflows, Qt6/PySide6 rendering, and reproducible point-sounding tools. It keeps the familiar SPC-style skew-T, hodograph, hazard, and derived-parameter views while adding clean command-line entry points, bundled resources, and a test-backed decoder/extractor layer.
en-US.name: SHARPpy-Reimagined
en-US.releaseNotes:
ECAPE now uses a native Rust workspace, reducing the delay and initial memory use when displaying the first sounding. Scientific reference checks, missing-data behavior and the existing CAPE bound remain covered by the release tests.

In the recorded local UHD comparison, the first-render median improved from 5.15 s to 3.37 s, with about 160 MiB less initial peak working set. Repeated-render timings were essentially unchanged. Results depend on the machine and workload; see the measurement method and limits.

This patch also includes the public-updater acceptance check for the existing install review.

- Fix public updater acceptance confirmation by @ShianMike in #130
- perf: accelerate first sounding display with native ECAPE by @ShianMike in #131
- Release v3.5.1: faster first sounding display by @ShianMike in #132
